proposals.title: Martin Haugh — The Black–Scholes Model (2016)
proposals.use: Further reading on stock/cash replication, constant continuous dividend yield, call/put formulas and the distinction between delta and risk-neutral exercise probability. Original chapter proofs, numbers and problems are independently developed.
proposals.verification: Actual primary author PDF retrieved. Header identifies 2016; inspected Section 1 on pages 1–3, volatility-surface setup on pages 3–4, and parity/delta on pages 6–7. Scope is mathematical teaching, not present-day executable market conventions. The chapter explicitly discounts gains and dated dividends, and states its own growth/admissibility class instead of adopting informal universal martingale or boundary claims.

proposals.title: Martin Haugh — Introduction to Stochastic Calculus for Diffusions (Fall 2013)
proposals.use: Further study on constant exponential-normal tilts, the additional hypotheses for general Girsanov, self-financing product terms and continuously reinvested dividends. This chapter proves only its finite-horizon constant-coefficient case and vanilla pricing uniqueness.
proposals.verification: Actual primary author PDF retrieved; cover/header and Sections 12–13 on pages 15–19 inspected. General theorem's Novikov footnote, constant-drift density-factorization discussion, self-financing product identity and dividend reinvestment inspected. No unqualified general FTAP, martingale-representation or local-martingale-to-martingale implication adopted; explicit lognormal mean/variance derived in the chapter rather than relying on the source's abbreviated terminal-distribution line.

proposals.title: Vasily Strela / MIT OpenCourseWare — Lecture 19: Black–Scholes Formula, Risk-neutral Valuation, 18.S096 (Fall 2013 transcript)
proposals.use: Alternative primary teaching exposition of the replication-to-PDE route, terminal/boundary data and the distinction between a common volatility model and strike-specific implied volatilities. No source examples or historical quotes reproduced.
proposals.verification: Official course resource and actual transcript PDF retrieved; pages 7–12 inspected for continuous-time assumptions, Ito replication, boundary discussion, risk-neutral expectation and constant-volatility interpretation. Lecture is historical; transcript's conversational mathematical shortcuts are not used as proof or current trading specifications.

scope_limit: Source-body inspection supports the stated method scope. The original proofs and lab require author and coordinator review; retrieval is not independent human certification. No current market data, discrete-dividend exact pricing claim or general stochastic-premium theorem is asserted.
